analysis.title: GS Blekos - ECB Recap, AI & Jobs, Haleon, Europe Industrials, Europe Retail, Adidas, TotalEnergies, HelleniQ, ASM International, Neste, Amazon, Intel, Sandisk (30 Oct 2026)
key_insights: GS maintains its forecast for one more ECB hike at the December meeting. More acute sovereign stress could lead the Council to hold, but the required tightening in financial conditions would likely need to be large given ongoing energy pressures.
GS sees an additional ECB hike in March as possible if energy prices keep rising, but sees a significant hurdle to speeding up the pace of hikes.

GS research finds workers displaced from AI-exposed jobs take about a month longer to find new jobs and are roughly 10pp more likely to remain unemployed a year after displacement, comparable to earlier waves of technological change.
Haleon reported Q3 organic sales growth of 2.6%, below company-compiled consensus of +3.2%, and cut guidance. GS cut EPS by 3%.

Haleon's guidance cut stems from two events not previously communicated: a halt to Centrum OTC imports into China (c.£75m FY25 sales, c.70bps full-year headwind) and a voluntary LatAm route-to-market change (£15-20m Q4 sales headwind).
Haleon's Asia Pacific organic growth was +3.9% and Europe was -0.6%. Oral Health grew +8.8% and is 38% of group 9M sales.
GS Europe Multi-Industry heatmap shows a broadly stable picture across regions. Sequential improvement is concentrated in data center/semis, while marine, rail and autos have deteriorated.
GS changed estimates and price targets for ABB, Atlas Copco, Konecranes, Nexans, Schindler, Signify and SKF. 2027 orders/sales/adj. EBIT move by about 1%/1%/1% on average.
GS UK HAC (Europe Retail) update: Budget impact is minimal in the near term. 2027E HAC growth is cut to +1.4% from +1.9%, and 2026E is raised to +3.5% from +2.1%.

Adidas 3Q26: apparel grew +19% cFX yoy (originals apparel +45%), Running +19%, Football +13%, Training +17%. Lifestyle footwear is challenged by excess US and Europe wholesale inventory, leaving footwear growth flat. Management sees the lifestyle footwear market possibly strengthening in 2H27. GS keeps a €180 target and Neutral.

TotalEnergies 3Q26: adjusted net income US$9.1bn (2% above company-compiled consensus of US$8.9bn) and OCF pre-OWC US$12.3bn (1% above US$12.1bn consensus). Strong refining and gas trading drove c.US$6bn net debt reduction, and quarterly buybacks step up to US$2.5bn. GS stays Neutral on relative valuation.

GS downgrades HelleniQ Energy to Neutral from Buy with the €20.0 target unchanged. At €18.71 the target implies 7% upside versus a 30% average for GS Buy-rated EU Energy names. Fundamentals stay positive, with c.50% middle distillates exposure.

ASM International: GS updates estimates and 12M PT after 3Q26. Advanced Logic/Foundry is expected to be the key 2027 growth driver, HBM-related capacity supports memory demand, gross margin outlook is constructive despite component-cost inflation, and China demand is robust, though the MATCH Act implications are unclear.

Neste 3Q26: comparable group EBITDA €1,555mn, 29% above Vara consensus of €1,202mn. Renewable Products EBITDA was €1,011mn (20% above consensus) and Oil Products was €504mn (48% above), with record Renewable Products volumes. GS stays Buy.

GS lists Amazon Q3'26 review (AWS revenue growth and operating margin trajectory framed as key to long-term fundamentals, compelling risk/reward), Intel (servers very strong, PC weakness likely a setback for the stock) and SanDisk (tight supply/demand drives estimates as datacenter exposure rises). Only headlines are given.

Adidas 3Q26 shows apparel momentum but lifestyle footwear stays challenged. Investors are cautious pending a footwear inflection.
TotalEnergies beat consensus on adjusted net income and OCF. GS stays Neutral on relative valuation.
Neste's 3Q26 EBITDA was 29% above consensus, driven by Oil Products and record Renewable Products volumes.
Haleon cut guidance on the China Centrum OTC import halt and a LatAm route-to-market change. GS cut EPS by 3%.
GS updated estimates and the 12M PT after 3Q26, citing leading-edge Logic/Foundry demand. The new target is not stated in the text.
GS headline calls risk/reward compelling from current levels, with AWS revenue growth and operating margin trajectory as key narratives.
Servers are very strong, but PC weakness is likely a setback for the stock.
Tight supply/demand conditions drive estimates as datacenter exposure moves higher.

sector_views.rationale: GS sees a more balanced risk-reward in refiners after a strong re-rating, and stays Neutral on TotalEnergies on relative valuation. Neste is rated Buy.
Sequential improvement in the Europe industrials heatmap is concentrated in DC/semis. ASM sees Advanced Logic/Foundry and HBM-related demand.
The heatmap shows deterioration in marine, rail and autos.
Haleon's guidance cut stems from China and LatAm headwinds, while Oral Health stays strong.

earnings_insights: Haleon Q3 (reported): organic sales growth 2.6% vs company-compiled consensus +3.2%. Asia Pacific +3.9%, Europe -0.6%, Oral Health +8.8%. GS cut EPS by 3%.
Adidas 3Q26 (reported): apparel +19% cFX yoy, originals apparel +45%, Running +19%, Football +13%, Training +17%, overall footwear flat.
TotalEnergies 3Q26 (reported 10/29): adjusted net income US$9.1bn vs company-compiled consensus US$8.9bn. OCF (pre-OWC) US$12.3bn vs consensus US$12.1bn. Buybacks step up to US$2.5bn per quarter.
Neste 3Q26 (reported): comparable group EBITDA €1,555mn vs Vara consensus €1,202mn. Renewable Products EBITDA €1,011mn (20% above consensus), Oil Products EBITDA €504mn (48% above consensus).
ASM International 3Q26 (reported): call takeaways point to Advanced Logic/Foundry as the 2027 growth driver and constructive gross margin despite component-cost inflation.
Europe Multi-Industry: 3Q26 heatmap. Estimate changes for ABB, Atlas Copco, Konecranes, Nexans, Schindler, Signify and SKF move 2027 orders/sales/adj. EBIT by about 1% on average.
